newsitem.title: USA: Comsat seeks $20 million in damages from ex-CEO.
newsitem.headline: Comsat seeks $20 million in damages from ex-CEO.

text.p: Comsat Corp. said Thursday it sued its former chief executive, Bruce Crockett, alleging a scheme linking him with businessman Herbert Denton and two companies that proposed a fight for control of Comsat.
Comsat, a global provider of communications services and products, is seeking over $20 million in damages and injunctive relief from the defendants.
The defendants include Providence Capital Inc. and Wyser-Pratte Inc., and a number of unidentified individuals.
Crockett and the other defendants were not immediately available for comment.

Comsat said the individuals were acting on behalf of a larger unidentified group which aimed to generate short-term, speculative profits by threatening a proxy contest for control of Bethesda, Md.-based Comsat.
Comsat said Crockett allegedly violated a 1996 termination contract in which he agreed not to disparage, compete with or disclose confidential information about Comsat to third parties.

Comsat said Crockett was forced to resign from the company in July 1996 to avoid being fired for the failure of his diversification strategy -- the source of most of the criticism Comsat now faces from shareholders who are threatening the proxy contest.
Comsat's stock fell $2.125 to $20.25 on the New York Stock Exchange in afternoon trading.
